about:
Leclerc Foods traces its roots to 1905 in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, Quebec, where the Leclerc family began baking cookies. Now a fifth-generation family-owned business, the company operates its U.S. headquarters from Kingsport, Tennessee, while maintaining its global headquarters in Quebec. What started as a small artisanal bakery has grown into a major North American food manufacturer with eight production facilities across Canada and the United States.

The company produces cookies, snack bars, and crackers at high volume — 8,000 snack bars per minute, roughly 1 billion cookies annually, and 16 million kilograms of flour processed each year. Its plants include dedicated peanut-free and gluten-free lines, supported by an in-house Health and Wellness Laboratory that develops new formulations. The network spans facilities in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, Hawkesbury, Cornwall, and Brockville (Ontario), Montgomery (Pennsylvania), and two sites in Kingsport (Tennessee).

Leclerc serves the food-service channel, retail grocery, and the broader agrifood industry. Its Food Service division supplies operators with portion-controlled and bulk products, while branded lines such as Célébration, Go Pure, and Tradition 1905 reach consumers through retail. The company also emphasizes community engagement through its Citizen Enterprise initiatives.

Leclerc differentiates itself through five generations of family stewardship, a commitment to premium ingredients, and continuous innovation via its wellness lab. The company cites authenticity, respect, innovation, commitment, and enjoyment as core values that guide daily operations and product development.
